representativeRepos.readmeText:
Impeccable

 The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder , review with critique and audit , and catch AI slop before it ships.

 From your project root:

 npx impeccable install

 Reload your coding tool, then run /impeccable init in your agent ( $impeccable init on Codex).

 Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at impeccable.style/docs .

 Without Impeccable
 With Impeccable

 Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water.

 For a full project, see the Neo Mirai case study : a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page.

 Why

 Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects.

- Words for what you want. "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. /impeccable bolder the pricing cards loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target.

- A reviewer. critique scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. audit checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish).

- A slop detector. 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key.

 Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see Build something new for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component:

 /impeccable critique the pricing cards

 How it works

 Run /impeccable init once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes PRODUCT.md . Every later command reads it. Run /impeccable document to capture your existing visual system in DESIGN.md , so changes stay on-brand. More on context files .

 Then name a command and a target:

 /impeccable critique the onboarding flow
/impeccable quieter the landing page
/impeccable polish settings
/impeccable harden checkout

 Or just describe what you want: /impeccable redo this hero section . Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with /impeccable pin audit to get /audit as its own shortcut.

 24 commands

 Commands

 Steer
 bolder amplifies safe designs · quieter tones down loud ones · distill removes what the page doesn't need · colorize brings color to a gray interface · typeset fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · layout fixes spacing and rhythm · animate adds transitions and interaction feedback · delight adds personality · overdrive goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects

 Review
 critique is a scored UX review · audit is a technical quality report

 Finish
 polish is the final pass before shipping · harden covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · clarify rewrites unclear copy · adapt handles screen sizes and devices · optimize fixes loading and rendering performance · onboard designs first-run flows and empty states

 Iterate live
 live lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · generate produces variants of a named element without manual picking

 Plan and set up
 shape plans UX before code · init writes PRODUCT.md · document writes DESIGN.md · extract pulls repeated patterns into your design system

 The 24th, craft , is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type /impeccable alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: impeccable.style/docs .

 On Codex, open /skills or type $impeccable instead of the slash command.

 Live mode

 /impeccable live opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. Iterate in the browser .

 Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your package.json 's optional impeccable:manual-edit-validate script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo.

 Three ways to run the detector

 In your agent. The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. Automatic design checks .

 In CI or your terminal. The CLI needs no agent:

 npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory
npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge)
npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output
npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations
npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description

 Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173 .

 Exit code 2 means findings, 1 means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font" . To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: <!-- impeccable-disable overused-font: exported brand doc --> . Run a detector scan · Configuration and ignores .

 In your browser. The Chrome extension overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. Review with a visual overlay .

 Installation

 npx impeccable install

 The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. npx impeccable update refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass --providers=claude,codex,cursor and --scope=project|global .

 Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open /hooks and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run /hooks-trust or launch with --trust . In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook once. Allow the hook in your harness .

 Node is only needed for npx . The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into ~/.impeccable/bin/ .

 Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins
 Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable , then open /plugin and install Impeccable.

 GitHub Copilot in VS Code: install Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace or run code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable . Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. Details .

 Grok Build: grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust installs the skill, agents, and hook.

 Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team)
 git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable
npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor

 Commit .gitmodules , the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run git submodule update --init --recursive . To upgrade, run git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable , rerun the link command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass --force .

 Manual copy, no Node required
 Download the ZIP for your tool from impeccable.style , or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy skills/impeccable from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder.

 For example: mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/ .

 Notes:

- A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run npx impeccable install to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path.

- OpenCode also needs .opencode/commands/impeccable.md copied into your project's .opencode/commands/ to provide /impeccable .

- Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run hermes skills trust from the project root. Global installs need no trust step.

- Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the Cursor and Gemini CLI skills docs.

- Restart Trae after copying.

- impeccable install and update manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when DSH_HOME is inside your home directory.

 Project files and git

 Impeccable writes its working files under .impeccable/ . A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: config.json , live/config.json , design.json , surfaces/*.md , and critique/*.md . Keep PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state.

 Copy the .gitignore entries
 # impeccable-ignore-start
 # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides.
 # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace.
 # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json,
 # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md.
 ** / .impeccable / config.local.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.cache.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.pending.json
 ** / .impeccable / * .png
 ** / .impeccable / review /
 ** / .impeccable / questions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / server.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / sessions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / previews /

 ** / .impeccable / live / cache /
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-apply-transaction.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-events.jsonl
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-evidence /
 ** / .impeccable / live / pending-manual-edits.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / * .png
 # impeccable-ignore-end

 The folders that hold decision-round state ( .impeccable/questions/ , .impeccable/mocks/worlds/ ) also ignore themselves. A .gitignore can't untrack a file git already tracks; if you committed one earlier, run git rm --cached <path> .

 Good to know

 Build path. For new landing pages and showcase surfaces, Impeccable can generate a full-fidelity comp first and build to match it (bolder, slower), or build straight in code (leaner, faster). App screens and documents are always built in code. init asks once and saves the answer as buildPath in .impeccable/...

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Orkas

 An open-source team of AI agents on your desktop — it turns your goals into finished work and keeps it moving.

 Orkas is an open-source (MIT), local-first multi-agent desktop app — an AI assistant that works as a team. Tell the Commander what you need: it finishes many tasks on its own, and for bigger work it plans the steps and brings in specialist agents along with the coding and personal agents you already use — Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent — to work on it together.

 Orkas is built to keep a project moving, not just answer one prompt. A project holds the goal, rules, memory and files, so every new conversation picks up where the last one left off. To-dos split the work between people and agents, Auto-advance lets the team take on the next to-do by itself, and scheduled automations repeat routine work hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. All your data stays on your computer, and finished work comes back for your review — so you can trust Orkas with the ongoing work of your business.

 ⬇ Download Orkas for macOS & Windows — free, with 500 credits for the built-in Orkas model, so you don't need an API key to start. Prefer your own keys? Claude · OpenAI · Gemini · DeepSeek · Kimi · GLM · Qwen · MiniMax · Doubao, or a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

 English · 简体中文

 orkas-demo.mp4

 What the team delivers

- Videos, voice-overs and images — VideoStudio, VoiceStudio, ImageStudio

- Research reports, SEO audits and market analysis — DeepResearcher, SeoGeoAgent, StockAnalyser

- Posts, articles, newsletters and slide decks — ContentWriter, PptMaker

- Websites, UI and code — UIDesigner, ProductDeveloper

- Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files — OfficeWorker

- E-commerce work — product research, listings, review analysis, sales analysis and catalog changes, from five e-commerce agents

- Complex work that takes several agents — the Commander splits it up, hands each part to the right agent and combines the results; for example, market research that becomes a report, a slide deck and a launch video

 16 specialists ship with the app, each with its own skills, memory and tools. Browse 30+ agents in the agent marketplace , or describe the role you need and the Commander builds a custom agent for you.

 All 16 built-in agents

 Area
 Agent
 What it delivers

 Research & analysis
 DeepResearcher
 Evidence-grounded research with verified sources, flagged contradictions and an auditable report

 SeoGeoAgent
 Give it a URL — technical audit, content quality, Core Web Vitals, AI-answer (GEO) citability, ranked fix list

 StockAnalyser
 Equity research, factor screens, backtests and portfolio risk checks, with traceable dashboards

 Content & media
 ContentWriter
 Publish-ready posts, articles, newsletters and case studies from a goal, sources or a rough draft

 PptMaker
 Editable, reviewable PPTX decks from a topic, outline or document

 ImageStudio
 Posters, covers, social images and infographics

 VideoStudio
 Narration, AI presenters, captions and dubbing, highlight clips, localization, and reference-video recreation with your own content and footage

 VoiceStudio
 Narration, multi-voice audio, transcripts and subtitles, audio editing and mixing

 UIDesigner
 Editable, HTML-first UI from product goals, PRDs, screenshots or Figma material

 Build & office
 ProductDeveloper
 Repo-aware engineering — implement a PRD, fix bugs, refactor, review, with verifiable results

 OfficeWorker
 Create, edit, check and deliver Word / Excel / PowerPoint / PDF files, one at a time or in batches

 E-commerce
 ECommerceResearcher
 Product selection by budget, market and sourcing limits — candidates, rejection reasons, validation plans

 ECommerceWriter
 Titles, detail pages, FAQs, image copy and video scripts in your brand voice

 ECommerceReviewer
 Review and reputation analysis — customer themes, root causes of bad reviews, priorities

 ECommerceAnalyzer
 Sales, profit, ads, refunds and inventory from your exports — reconciled metrics and decisions

 ECommerceOperator
 Plans catalog, price, promotion and inventory changes; executes only through tools you connect

 More on each agent → orkas.ai/agents

 Recreate a reference video with your own content

 VideoStudio can recreate a viral video's narrative structure, visual style and editing pace using your own product, script and footage. Supply a reference video file and your assets: the agent analyzes the hook, information order, visual beats and call to action, then proposes what to preserve and what to replace before production.

 This works best for motion-graphic explainers, SaaS or app demos, and product ads built from your existing footage. Locally authored text, captions, narration and clips can be revised separately; text baked into AI-generated footage requires changing that footage.

 "Use reference.mp4 as a reference for a 30-second vertical promo. Keep its hook, typography and pacing, replace the content with my product and screen recordings, and show me the breakdown and plan first."

 Start with a video file the agent can read; social-platform share-link downloading is not built in. Exact camera moves, human performances and frame-by-frame matching are not guaranteed. See the reference-recreation workflow .

 Keep the work moving

 One task is a good start. Orkas is built for the work that keeps going.

- Projects — goals & rules, memory and files that every conversation in the project starts from, so you never brief from scratch.

- To-dos and Auto-advance — every project has a to-do list for people and agents; with Auto-advance on, the team picks up the next item on its own and brings finished work back for your review.

- Scheduled automations — run any task hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. Orkas runs on your computer. From v1.9, each automation catches up its most recent missed run within 12 hours when the computer wakes or Orkas starts.

- Connectors — Gmail, Google Calendar, Sheets and Drive, Notion, Slack, Shopify, Stripe and many more. By default, Orkas asks before it sends, posts or deletes anything.

- Apps — describe a tool and Orkas builds it as a local app inside the desktop app. In the packaged app, paid plans can also publish it as a web app with a public link.

- Shared projects (packaged app) — invite a teammate or VA, and give each to-do to a person or an agent.

 Note
 Shared projects, cloud sync and web-app publishing are only in the packaged app — the open-source build doesn't support them yet. To use them, download Orkas for macOS & Windows (free, with 500 credits to start).

 Voice input also works in the source build. Configure an Orkas API Key in Settings → Models , then click the microphone beside a composer. Allow microphone access when prompted. Audio is sent to Orkas for recognition and uses the key owner’s Orkas credits. Click again to stop, review the text, and send it yourself. If access was denied, enable the microphone in your system settings.

 Run Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent together

 Orkas runs the CLI agents you already have installed as local sessions, next to its own specialists — the coding agents Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode , and the personal agents OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent . The Commander hands each one the part it's best at and keeps one plan across all of them, so a single chat can fix the bug, review the change and draft the release note. Open-source tools such as HyperFrames plug in the same way.

 Using Claude Code and Codex together →

 Why Orkas

- A Commander that plans, delegates and does the rest — it breaks down goals, picks the right agents, skills, connectors and tools, and handles analysis, writing, research and file work itself when no specialist is a better fit.

- Local-first by design — conversations, files, knowledge bases and custom agents stay on your disk by default. Cloud sync is optional in the packaged app. With your own keys, model calls go straight from your machine to the provider; the built-in Orkas model runs through Orkas's managed model service.

- Any model, switch any time — the Commander and built-in agents share one model setting: the built-in Orkas model, your own provider, or a local endpoint. External CLI agents keep their own model settings.

- Agents that get better — each agent keeps private skills and memory. Background reviews examine new activity when the app is idle and can refine self-assessment, reusable methods and learned skills.

- Open source, no black box — MIT licensed. Read exactly what Orkas and every agent and skill do.

 ⭐ If Orkas is useful to you, a star helps more people find the project.

 What people use it for

- Marketing content — launch videos, product pages, posts and newsletters in your voice. Content writing · Videos

- Store operations — weekly sales briefs, review replies, listings and competitor checks. E-commerce

- Research and reports — sourced reports and decks, on demand or every week. Research · Data analysis

- Chat with your documents — answers grounded in your own files, with citations back to the source passages. Chat with documents

- Client work — meeting briefs, monthly client reports and update decks in your template. Monthly client report template

- Product launch — landing pages, bug fixes with tests, changelogs and launch posts. Developers

- Build an app — quote calculators, booking forms, internal tools. Build apps

- Small teams — one project for people and agents. Small teams

 How Orkas compares

 Tool
 What it is
 How Orkas differs

 Claude Code
 Anthropic's agentic coding tool — in the terminal, IDE, desktop and web, built on Claude models.
 Not either-or: Orkas runs Claude Code as one of its agents. Around it, Orkas adds a model-agnostic team for the work beyond code — research, content, video and more — with projects, to-dos and automations that keep it moving. Orkas vs Claude Code →

 Codex
 OpenAI's coding agent — in the terminal, your editor and the cloud.
 Not either-or: Orkas runs Codex as one of its agents, next to Claude Code and OpenCode. The Commander can hand the coding to Codex and the review to another agent, then cover the non-code half of a release — docs, launch posts and videos. Orkas vs Codex →

 LangChain
 A developer framework/library for building LLM apps and agents — code-first, embedded in your own Python/JS app.
 Orkas is a desktop app you direct through chat, not by writing orchestration code. Data stays local by default.

 CrewAI
 A Python framework for orchestrating role-playing autonomous agents — you define crews and agents in code.
 Orkas brings multi-agent orchestration into a desktop app, with projects, to-dos, automations and per-agent self-improvement built in.

 OpenClaw
 A personal-agent platform with messaging integrations, multi-agent routing and sub-agents.
 Orkas provides a desktop workspace for finished deliverables, with built-in specialists and coordination across Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other CLI agents. OpenClaw can join that workflow as a CLI agent.

 Hermes-Agent
 Nous Research's self-improving agent — one agent with memory and skills, available as a CLI, a messaging gateway and a desktop app.
 Orkas coordinates a team: the Commander directs many specialists and other CLI agents, and Hermes-Agent plugs in as one of them.

 Orkas is for you if you want a team of agents rather than one assistant, work that keeps moving across days, and your data, keys and agents on your own disk.

 Network

 In general, what do you need in order to communicate?

- A common language (for the two ends to understand)

- A way to address who you want to communicate with

- A Connection (so the content of the communication can reach the recipients)

 What is TCP/IP?

 A set of protocols that define how two or more devices can communicate with each other.

 To learn more about TCP/IP, read here

 What is Ethernet?

 Ethernet simply refers to the most common type of Local Area Network (LAN) used today. A LAN—in contrast to a WAN (Wide Area Network), which spans a larger geographical area—is a connected network of computers in a small area, like your office, college campus, or even home.

 What is a MAC address? What is it used for?

 A MAC address is a unique identification number or code used to identify individual devices on the network.

 Packets that are sent on the ethernet are always coming from a MAC address and sent to a MAC address. If a network adapter is receiving a packet, it is comparing the packet’s destination MAC address to the adapter’s own MAC address.

 When is this MAC address used?: ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff

 When a device sends a packet to the broadcast MAC address (FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF​), it is delivered to all stations on the local network. Ethernet broadcasts are used to resolve IP addresses to MAC addresses (by ARP) at the data link layer.

 What is an IP address?

 An Internet Protocol address (IP address) is a numerical label assigned to each device connected to a computer network that uses the Internet Protocol for communication.An IP address serves two main functions: host or network interface identification and location addressing.

 Explain the subnet mask and give an example

 A Subnet mask is a 32-bit number that masks an IP address and divides the IP addresses into network addresses and host addresses. Subnet Mask is made by setting network bits to all "1"s and setting host bits to all "0"s. Within a given network, out of the total usable host addresses, two are always reserved for specific purposes and cannot be allocated to any host. These are the first address, which is reserved as a network address (a.k.a network ID), and the last address used for network broadcast.

 Example

 What is a private IP address? In which scenarios/system designs, one should use it?

Private IP addresses are assigned to the hosts in the same network to communicate with one another. As the name "private" suggests, the devices having the private IP addresses assigned can't be reached by the devices from any external network. For example, if I am living in a hostel and I want my hostel mates to join the game server I have hosted, I will ask them to join via my server's private IP address, since the network is local to the hostel.

 What is a public IP address? In which scenarios/system designs, one should use it?

A public IP address is a public-facing IP address. In the event that you were hosting a game server that you want your friends to join, you will give your friends your public IP address to allow their computers to identify and locate your network and server in order for the connection to take place. One time that you would not need to use a public-facing IP address is in the event that you were playing with friends who were connected to the same network as you, in that case, you would use a private IP address. In order for someone to be able to connect to your server that is located internally, you will have to set up a port forward to tell your router to allow traffic from the public domain into your network and vice versa.

 Explain the OSI model. What layers there are? What each layer is responsible for?

- Application: user end (HTTP is here)

- Presentation: establishes context between application-layer entities (Encryption is here)

- Session: establishes, manages, and terminates the connections

- Transport: transfers variable-length data sequences from a source to a destination host (TCP & UDP are here)

- Network: transfers datagrams from one network to another (IP is here)

- Data link: provides a link between two directly connected nodes (MAC is here)

- Physical: the electrical and physical spec of the data connection (Bits are here)

 You can read more about the OSI model in penguintutor.com

 For each of the following determines to which OSI layer it belongs:

- Error correction

- Packets routing

- Cables and electrical signals

- MAC address

- IP address

- Terminate connections

- 3 way handshake

- Error correction - Data link

- Packets routing - Network

- Cables and electrical signals - Physical

- MAC address - Data link

- IP address - Network

- Terminate connections - Session

 - 3-way handshake - Transport

 What delivery schemes are you familiar with?

 Unicast: One-to-one communication where there is one sender and one receiver.

 Broadcast: Sending a message to everyone in the network. The address ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff is used for broadcasting.
Two common protocols which use broadcast are ARP and DHCP.

 Multicast: Sending a message to a group of subscribers. It can be one-to-many or many-to-many.

 What is CSMA/CD? Is it used in modern ethernet networks?

 CSMA/CD stands for Carrier Sense Multiple Access / Collision Detection.
Its primary focus is to manage access to a shared medium/bus where only one host can transmit at a given point in time.

 CSMA/CD algorithm:

- Before sending a frame, it checks whether another host is already transmitting a frame.

- If no one is transmitting, it starts transmitting the frame.

- If two hosts transmit at the same time, we have a collision.

- Both hosts stop sending the frame and they send everyone a 'jam signal' notifying everyone that a collision occurred

- They are waiting for a random time before sending it again

 - Once each host waited for a random time, they try to send the frame again and so the cycle starts again

 Describe the following network devices and the difference between them:

- router

- switch

- hub

 A router, switch, and hub are all network devices used to connect devices in a local area network (LAN). However, each device operates differently and has its specific use cases. Here is a brief description of each device and the differences between them:

- Router: a network device that connects multiple network segments together. It operates at the network layer (Layer 3) of the OSI model and uses routing protocols to direct data between networks. Routers use IP addresses to identify devices and route data packets to the correct destination.

- Switch: a network device that connects multiple devices on a LAN. It operates at the data link layer (Layer 2) of the OSI model and uses MAC addresses to identify devices and direct data packets to the correct destination. Switches allow devices on the same network to communicate with each other more efficiently and can prevent data collisions that can occur when multiple devices send data simultaneously.

 - Hub: a network device that connects multiple devices through a single cable and is used to connect multiple devices without segmenting a network. However, unlike a switch, it operates at the physical layer (Layer 1) of the OSI model and simply broadcasts data packets to all devices connected to it, regardless of whether the device is the intended recipient or not. This means that data collisions can occur, and the network's efficiency can suffer as a result. Hubs are generally not used in modern network setups, as switches are more efficient and provide better network performance.

 What is a "Collision Domain"?

A collision domain is a network segment in which devices can potentially interfere with each other by attempting to transmit data at the same time. When two devices transmit data at the same time, it can cause a collision, resulting in lost or corrupted data. In a collision domain, all devices share the same bandwidth, and any device can potentially interfere with the transmission of data by other devices.

 What is a "Broadcast Domain"?

A broadcast domain is a network segment in which all devices can communicate with each other by sending broadcast messages. A broadcast message is a message that is sent to all devices in a network rather than a specific device. In a broadcast domain, all devices can receive and process broadcast messages, regardless of whether the message was intended for them or not.

 three computers connected to a switch. How many collision domains are there? How many broadcast domains?

 Three collision domains and one broadcast domain

 How does a router work?

 A router is a physical or virtual appliance that passes information between two or more packet-switched computer networks. A router inspects a given data packet's destination Internet Protocol address (IP address), calculates the best way for it to reach its destination, and then forwards it accordingly.

 What is NAT?

 Network Address Translation (NAT) is a process in which one or more local IP addresses are translated into one or more Global IP address and vice versa in order to provide Internet access to the local hosts.

 What is a proxy? How does it work? What do we need it for?

 A proxy server acts as a gateway between you and the internet. It’s an intermediary server separating end users from the websites they browse.

 If you’re using a proxy server, internet traffic flows through the proxy server on its way to the address you requested. The request then comes back through that same proxy server (there are exceptions to this rule), and then the proxy server forwards the data received from the website to you.

 Proxy servers provide varying levels of functionality, security, and privacy depending on your use case, needs, or company policy.

 What is TCP? How does it work? What is the 3-way handshake?

 TCP 3-way handshake or three-way handshake is a process that is used in a TCP/IP network to make a connection between server and client.

 A three-way handshake is primarily used to create a TCP socket connection. It works when:

- A client node sends an SYN data packet over an IP network to a server on the same or an external network. The objective of this packet is to ask/infer if the server is open for new connections.

- The target server must have open ports that can accept and initiate new connections. When the server receives the SYN packet from the client node, it responds and returns a confirmation receipt – the ACK packet or SYN/ACK packet.

 - The client node receives the SYN/ACK from the server and responds with an ACK packet.

readmeText:
Orkas

 An open-source team of AI agents on your desktop — it turns your goals into finished work and keeps it moving.

 Orkas is an open-source (MIT), local-first multi-agent desktop app — an AI assistant that works as a team. Tell the Commander what you need: it finishes many tasks on its own, and for bigger work it plans the steps and brings in specialist agents along with the coding and personal agents you already use — Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent — to work on it together.

 Orkas is built to keep a project moving, not just answer one prompt. A project holds the goal, rules, memory and files, so every new conversation picks up where the last one left off. To-dos split the work between people and agents, Auto-advance lets the team take on the next to-do by itself, and scheduled automations repeat routine work hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. All your data stays on your computer, and finished work comes back for your review — so you can trust Orkas with the ongoing work of your business.

 ⬇ Download Orkas for macOS & Windows — free, with 500 credits for the built-in Orkas model, so you don't need an API key to start. Prefer your own keys? Claude · OpenAI · Gemini · DeepSeek · Kimi · GLM · Qwen · MiniMax · Doubao, or a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

 English · 简体中文

 orkas-demo.mp4

 What the team delivers

- Videos, voice-overs and images — VideoStudio, VoiceStudio, ImageStudio

- Research reports, SEO audits and market analysis — DeepResearcher, SeoGeoAgent, StockAnalyser

- Posts, articles, newsletters and slide decks — ContentWriter, PptMaker

- Websites, UI and code — UIDesigner, ProductDeveloper

- Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files — OfficeWorker

- E-commerce work — product research, listings, review analysis, sales analysis and catalog changes, from five e-commerce agents

- Complex work that takes several agents — the Commander splits it up, hands each part to the right agent and combines the results; for example, market research that becomes a report, a slide deck and a launch video

 16 specialists ship with the app, each with its own skills, memory and tools. Browse 30+ agents in the agent marketplace , or describe the role you need and the Commander builds a custom agent for you.

 All 16 built-in agents

 Area
 Agent
 What it delivers

 Research & analysis
 DeepResearcher
 Evidence-grounded research with verified sources, flagged contradictions and an auditable report

 SeoGeoAgent
 Give it a URL — technical audit, content quality, Core Web Vitals, AI-answer (GEO) citability, ranked fix list

 StockAnalyser
 Equity research, factor screens, backtests and portfolio risk checks, with traceable dashboards

 Content & media
 ContentWriter
 Publish-ready posts, articles, newsletters and case studies from a goal, sources or a rough draft

 PptMaker
 Editable, reviewable PPTX decks from a topic, outline or document

 ImageStudio
 Posters, covers, social images and infographics

 VideoStudio
 Narration, AI presenters, captions and dubbing, highlight clips, localization, and reference-video recreation with your own content and footage

 VoiceStudio
 Narration, multi-voice audio, transcripts and subtitles, audio editing and mixing

 UIDesigner
 Editable, HTML-first UI from product goals, PRDs, screenshots or Figma material

 Build & office
 ProductDeveloper
 Repo-aware engineering — implement a PRD, fix bugs, refactor, review, with verifiable results

 OfficeWorker
 Create, edit, check and deliver Word / Excel / PowerPoint / PDF files, one at a time or in batches

 E-commerce
 ECommerceResearcher
 Product selection by budget, market and sourcing limits — candidates, rejection reasons, validation plans

 ECommerceWriter
 Titles, detail pages, FAQs, image copy and video scripts in your brand voice

 ECommerceReviewer
 Review and reputation analysis — customer themes, root causes of bad reviews, priorities

 ECommerceAnalyzer
 Sales, profit, ads, refunds and inventory from your exports — reconciled metrics and decisions

 ECommerceOperator
 Plans catalog, price, promotion and inventory changes; executes only through tools you connect

 More on each agent → orkas.ai/agents

 Recreate a reference video with your own content

 VideoStudio can recreate a viral video's narrative structure, visual style and editing pace using your own product, script and footage. Supply a reference video file and your assets: the agent analyzes the hook, information order, visual beats and call to action, then proposes what to preserve and what to replace before production.

 This works best for motion-graphic explainers, SaaS or app demos, and product ads built from your existing footage. Locally authored text, captions, narration and clips can be revised separately; text baked into AI-generated footage requires changing that footage.

 "Use reference.mp4 as a reference for a 30-second vertical promo. Keep its hook, typography and pacing, replace the content with my product and screen recordings, and show me the breakdown and plan first."

 Start with a video file the agent can read; social-platform share-link downloading is not built in. Exact camera moves, human performances and frame-by-frame matching are not guaranteed. See the reference-recreation workflow .

 Keep the work moving

 One task is a good start. Orkas is built for the work that keeps going.

- Projects — goals & rules, memory and files that every conversation in the project starts from, so you never brief from scratch.

- To-dos and Auto-advance — every project has a to-do list for people and agents; with Auto-advance on, the team picks up the next item on its own and brings finished work back for your review.

- Scheduled automations — run any task hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. Orkas runs on your computer. From v1.9, each automation catches up its most recent missed run within 12 hours when the computer wakes or Orkas starts.

- Connectors — Gmail, Google Calendar, Sheets and Drive, Notion, Slack, Shopify, Stripe and many more. By default, Orkas asks before it sends, posts or deletes anything.

- Apps — describe a tool and Orkas builds it as a local app inside the desktop app. In the packaged app, paid plans can also publish it as a web app with a public link.

- Shared projects (packaged app) — invite a teammate or VA, and give each to-do to a person or an agent.

 Note
 Shared projects, cloud sync and web-app publishing are only in the packaged app — the open-source build doesn't support them yet. To use them, download Orkas for macOS & Windows (free, with 500 credits to start).

 Voice input also works in the source build. Configure an Orkas API Key in Settings → Models , then click the microphone beside a composer. Allow microphone access when prompted. Audio is sent to Orkas for recognition and uses the key owner’s Orkas credits. Click again to stop, review the text, and send it yourself. If access was denied, enable the microphone in your system settings.

 Run Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent together

 Orkas runs the CLI agents you already have installed as local sessions, next to its own specialists — the coding agents Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode , and the personal agents OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent . The Commander hands each one the part it's best at and keeps one plan across all of them, so a single chat can fix the bug, review the change and draft the release note. Open-source tools such as HyperFrames plug in the same way.

 Using Claude Code and Codex together →

 Why Orkas

- A Commander that plans, delegates and does the rest — it breaks down goals, picks the right agents, skills, connectors and tools, and handles analysis, writing, research and file work itself when no specialist is a better fit.

- Local-first by design — conversations, files, knowledge bases and custom agents stay on your disk by default. Cloud sync is optional in the packaged app. With your own keys, model calls go straight from your machine to the provider; the built-in Orkas model runs through Orkas's managed model service.

- Any model, switch any time — the Commander and built-in agents share one model setting: the built-in Orkas model, your own provider, or a local endpoint. External CLI agents keep their own model settings.

- Agents that get better — each agent keeps private skills and memory. Background reviews examine new activity when the app is idle and can refine self-assessment, reusable methods and learned skills.

- Open source, no black box — MIT licensed. Read exactly what Orkas and every agent and skill do.

 ⭐ If Orkas is useful to you, a star helps more people find the project.

 Get it
 Download Orkas
 Quick start

 The download link detects your system and starts the right installer.

 What people use it for

- Marketing content — launch videos, product pages, posts and newsletters in your voice. Content writing · Videos

- Store operations — weekly sales briefs, review replies, listings and competitor checks. E-commerce

- Research and reports — sourced reports and decks, on demand or every week. Research · Data analysis

- Chat with your documents — answers grounded in your own files, with citations back to the source passages. Chat with documents

- Client work — meeting briefs, monthly client reports and update decks in your template. Monthly client report template

- Product launch — landing pages, bug fixes with tests, changelogs and launch posts. Developers

- Build an app — quote calculators, booking forms, internal tools. Build apps

- Small teams — one project for people and agents. Small teams

 How Orkas compares

 Tool
 What it is
 How Orkas differs

 Claude Code
 Anthropic's agentic coding tool — in the terminal, IDE, desktop and web, built on Claude models.
 Not either-or: Orkas runs Claude Code as one of its agents. Around it, Orkas adds a model-agnostic team for the work beyond code — research, content, video and more — with projects, to-dos and automations that keep it moving. Orkas vs Claude Code →

 Codex
 OpenAI's coding agent — in the terminal, your editor and the cloud.
 Not either-or: Orkas runs Codex as one of its agents, next to Claude Code and OpenCode. The Commander can hand the coding to Codex and the review to another agent, then cover the non-code half of a release — docs, launch posts and videos. Orkas vs Codex →

 LangChain
 A developer framework/library for building LLM apps and agents — code-first, embedded in your own Python/JS app.
 Orkas is a desktop app you direct through chat, not by writing orchestration code. Data stays local by default.

 CrewAI
 A Python framework for orchestrating role-playing autonomous agents — you define crews and agents in code.
 Orkas brings multi-agent orchestration into a desktop app, with projects, to-dos, automations and per-agent self-improvement built in.

 OpenClaw
 A personal-agent platform with messaging integrations, multi-agent routing and sub-agents.
 Orkas provides a desktop workspace for finished deliverables, with built-in specialists and coordination across Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other CLI agents. OpenClaw can join that workflow as a CLI agent.

 Hermes-Agent
 Nous Research's self-improving agent — one agent with memory and skills, available as a CLI, a messaging gateway and a desktop app.
 Orkas coordinates a team: the Commander directs many specialists and other CLI agents, and Hermes-Agent plugs in as one of them.

 Orkas is for you if you want a team of agents rather than one assistant, work that keeps moving across days, and your data, keys and agents on your own disk.

 Quick Start •
 How It Works •
 Search Tools •

 License

 Claude-Mem seamlessly preserves context across sessions by automatically capturing tool usage observations, generating semantic summaries, and making them available to future sessions. This enables Claude to maintain continuity of knowledge about projects even after sessions end or reconnect.

 Quick Start

 Install claude-mem for Grok Bot:

 npx claude-mem install --ide grok-bot

 Grok Bot has no host hooks, so we watch the chat log files. Default is CMEM Pro, the hosted memory. Local observer is opt-in: --provider host . Installing this plugin does not install Cursor.

 Awareness push pilot (LFG + Orifice): needle observations ( decision , bugfix , security_alert , sensitive ) are appended as dated - YYYY-MM-DD [awareness] … lines into that bot's memory/log/YYYY-MM.md . Grok Bot already re-reads the log from disk. This does not write profile.md , user-memory, or project memory. Disable with CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_ENABLED=false .

 Install with a single command:

 npx claude-mem install

 The installer sets everything up first, then asks you to sign in to claude-mem in your browser (email magic link — no card required). Signing in provisions a memory key for your account and unlocks the claude-mem observer with a 30 Day Free Trial : memory runs off-plan, so you get up to 100% more usage from your plan. When the free trial ends, memory automatically falls back to your Anthropic plan unless you subscribe. After sign-in you pick your memory provider — the claude-mem observer, your own OpenRouter or Gemini key, or your Anthropic plan.

 Prefer to skip the sign-in? Pass an explicit --provider flag, set CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false , or run in CI/non-interactive shells — the installer completes without any account interaction.

 Or install for OpenCode:

 npx claude-mem install --ide opencode

 This works with OpenCode 1.3.4 or later, including OpenCode 2. Restart OpenCode after installing.

 Or install for T3 Code (Codex and Claude Code providers):

 npx claude-mem install --ide t3code

 The installer discovers T3 Code's enabled providers, registers native Claude-Mem plugins in their configured homes, and supports T3-managed Codex. Restart T3 Code, trust the provider's hooks when prompted, and start a new thread. See the T3 Code integration guide for custom server settings, status, and removal.

 Or install for Antigravity CLI ( setup guide ):

 npx claude-mem install --ide antigravity

 Or install for OMP (Oh My Pi):

 npx claude-mem install --ide omp

 Or install the native Pi extension or DeepSeek Harness plugin:

 npx claude-mem install --ide pi
npx claude-mem install --ide dsh --dsh-profile tui

 Pi and DeepSeek Harness use the worker runtime. See native harness setup for capture, recall, and troubleshooting.

 Or install from the plugin marketplace inside Claude Code:

 /plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem

/plugin install claude-mem

 Restart Claude Code. Context from previous sessions will automatically appear in new sessions.

 Note: Claude-Mem is also published on npm, but npm install -g claude-mem installs the SDK/library only — it does not register the plugin hooks or set up the worker service. Always install via npx claude-mem install or the /plugin commands above.

 🦞 OpenClaw Gateway

 Install claude-mem as a persistent memory plugin on OpenClaw gateways with a single command:

 curl -fsSL https://install.cmem.ai/openclaw.sh | bash

 The installer handles dependencies, plugin setup, AI provider configuration, worker startup, and optional real-time observation feeds to Telegram, Discord, Slack, and more. See the OpenClaw Integration Guide for details.

 Key Features:

- 🧠 Persistent Memory - Context survives across sessions

- 📊 Progressive Disclosure - Layered memory retrieval with token cost visibility

- 🔍 Smart Search (Default) - Query your project history with the three-step mem-search skill

- 🖥️ Local My Work - Live requests, progress, human handoffs and a saved review queue at the worker URL printed on startup. Guide . Memory, sessions and settings remain at /viewer .

- 👥 TeamBrain - An optional shared workspace beside My Work, with real team work lists, member attribution and linked findings. Each person chooses what to share; personal requests and review notes stay separate. Set up a team .

- 💻 Claude Desktop Skill - Search memory from Claude Desktop conversations

- 🔒 Privacy Control - Use <private> tags to exclude sensitive content from storage

- 🖼️ Screenshots (opt-in, off by default) - Keep converted copies of tool screenshots under ~/.claude-mem/media-v1/ , upload them to cmem.ai only when Cloud Sync is on, and send them to the observer model only when image inference is separately enabled ( details )

- ⚙️ Context Configuration - Fine-grained control over what context gets injected

- 🤖 Automatic Operation - No manual intervention required

- 🔗 Citations - Reference past observations with IDs through the worker API or view all in the web viewer

 Documentation

 📚 View Full Documentation - Browse on official website

 Getting Started

- Installation Guide - Quick start & advanced installation

- Usage Guide - How Claude-Mem works automatically

- Search Tools - Query your project history with natural language

- Cloud Sync - Back up your memories to cmem.ai — no daemon, the worker syncs on write

 Best Practices

- Context Engineering - AI agent context optimization principles

- Progressive Disclosure - Philosophy behind Claude-Mem's context priming strategy

 Architecture

- Overview - System components & data flow

- Architecture Evolution - The journey from v3 to v5

- Hooks Architecture - How Claude-Mem uses lifecycle hooks

- Hooks Reference - Every hook entry explained

- Worker Service - HTTP API & Bun management

- Database - SQLite schema & FTS5 search

- Search Architecture - Hybrid search with Chroma vector database

 Configuration & Development

- Configuration - Environment variables & settings

- Development - Building, testing, contributing

- Troubleshooting - Common issues & solutions

 How It Works

 Core Components:

- Lifecycle Hooks - SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd. Each is one shell-free command, claude-mem hook claude-code <event> , run by a small launcher that the installer puts on PATH

- Smart Install - Cached dependency checker (Setup hook on claude --init / --maintenance , plus npx claude-mem install / repair )

- Worker Service - Local HTTP API with web viewer UI and search endpoints, managed by Bun

- SQLite Database - Stores sessions, observations, summaries

- mem-search Skill - Natural language queries with progressive disclosure

- Chroma Vector Database - Hybrid semantic + keyword search for intelligent context retrieval

 See Architecture Overview for details.

 MCP Search Tools

 Claude-Mem provides intelligent memory search through 4 MCP tools following a token-efficient 3-layer workflow pattern :

 The 3-Layer Workflow:

- search - Get compact index with IDs (~50-100 tokens/result)

- timeline - Get chronological context around interesting results

- get_observations - Fetch full details ONLY for filtered IDs (~500-1,000 tokens/result)

 How It Works:

- Claude uses MCP tools to search your memory

- Start with search to get an index of results

- Use timeline to see what was happening around specific observations

- Use get_observations to fetch full details for relevant IDs

- ~10x token savings by filtering before fetching details

 Available MCP Tools:

- search - Search memory index with full-text queries, filters by type/date/project

- timeline - Get chronological context around a specific observation or query

- get_observations - Fetch full observation details by IDs (always batch multiple IDs)

 Example Usage:

 // Step 1: Search for index
 search ( query = "authentication bug" , type = "bugfix" , limit = 10 )

 // Step 2: Review index, identify relevant IDs (e.g., #123, #456)

 // Step 3: Fetch full details
 get_observations ( ids = [ 123 , 456 ] )

 See Search Tools Guide for detailed examples.

 System Requirements

- Node.js : 20.0.0 or higher

- Claude Code : Latest version with plugin support

- Bun : JavaScript runtime and process manager (auto-installed if missing)

- uv : Python package manager for vector search (auto-installed if missing)

- SQLite 3 : For persistent storage (bundled)

 Windows Setup Notes

 If you see an error like:

 npm : The term ' npm ' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet

 Make sure Node.js and npm are installed and added to your PATH. Download the latest Node.js installer from https://nodejs.org and restart your terminal after installation.

 Claude Code hooks do not need Git Bash. Each hook runs claude-mem directly, and npx claude-mem install places that launcher at %LOCALAPPDATA%\claude-mem\bin\claude-mem.exe and adds the folder to your user Path. Restart your terminal or IDE afterwards so Claude Code picks up the new Path. If hooks report Executable not found in $PATH: "claude-mem" , run npx claude-mem doctor and see Troubleshooting .

 Configuration

 Settings are managed in ~/.claude-mem/settings.json (auto-created with defaults on first run). Configure AI model, worker port, data directory, log level, and context injection settings.

 To include observations from every harness in Claude Code and Codex SessionStart context, set "CLAUDE_MEM_SESSION_START_INCLUDE_ALL_SOURCES": "true" in that file, or enable Include all sources at session start in the viewer settings. The default is "false" , which limits startup context to the current harness. The observation count limit still applies across the selected sources.

 See the Configuration Guide for all available settings and examples.

 Mode & Language Configuration

 Claude-Mem supports multiple workflow modes and languages via the CLAUDE_MEM_MODE setting.

 This option controls both:

- The workflow behavior (e.g. code, chill, investigation)

- The language used in generated observations

 How to Configure

 Edit your settings file at ~/.claude-mem/settings.json :

 {
 "CLAUDE_MEM_MODE" : " code--zh "
}

 Modes are defined in plugin/modes/ . To see all available modes locally:

 ls ~ /.claude/plugins/marketplaces/thedotmack/plugin/modes/

 Available Modes

 Mode
 Description

 code
 Default English mode

 code--zh
 Simplified Chinese mode

 code--ja
 Japanese mode

 Language-specific modes follow the pattern code--[lang] where [lang] is the ISO 639-1 language code (e.g., zh for Chinese, ja for Japanese, es for Spanish).

 Note: code--zh (Simplified Chinese) is already built-in — no additional installation or plugin update is required.

 After Changing Mode

 Restart Claude Code to apply the new mode configuration.

 Development

 See the Development Guide for build instructions, testing, and contribution workflow.

 Troubleshooting

 If experiencing issues, describe the problem to Claude and the troubleshoot skill will automatically diagnose and provide fixes.

 See the Troubleshooting Guide for common issues and solutions.

 Bug Reports

 Create comprehensive bug reports with the automated generator:

 cd ~ /.claude/plugins/marketplaces/thedotmack
npm run bug-report

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Impeccable

 The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder , review with critique and audit , and catch AI slop before it ships.

 From your project root:

 npx impeccable install

 Reload your coding tool, then run /impeccable init in your agent ( $impeccable init on Codex).

 Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at impeccable.style/docs .

 Without Impeccable
 With Impeccable

 Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water.

 For a full project, see the Neo Mirai case study : a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page.

 Why

 Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects.

- Words for what you want. "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. /impeccable bolder the pricing cards loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target.

- A reviewer. critique scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. audit checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish).

- A slop detector. 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key.

 Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see Build something new for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component:

 /impeccable critique the pricing cards

 How it works

 Run /impeccable init once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes PRODUCT.md . Every later command reads it. Run /impeccable document to capture your existing visual system in DESIGN.md , so changes stay on-brand. More on context files .

 Then name a command and a target:

 /impeccable critique the onboarding flow
/impeccable quieter the landing page
/impeccable polish settings
/impeccable harden checkout

 Or just describe what you want: /impeccable redo this hero section . Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with /impeccable pin audit to get /audit as its own shortcut.

 24 commands

 Commands

 Steer
 bolder amplifies safe designs · quieter tones down loud ones · distill removes what the page doesn't need · colorize brings color to a gray interface · typeset fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · layout fixes spacing and rhythm · animate adds transitions and interaction feedback · delight adds personality · overdrive goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects

 Review
 critique is a scored UX review · audit is a technical quality report

 Finish
 polish is the final pass before shipping · harden covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · clarify rewrites unclear copy · adapt handles screen sizes and devices · optimize fixes loading and rendering performance · onboard designs first-run flows and empty states

 Iterate live
 live lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · generate produces variants of a named element without manual picking

 Plan and set up
 shape plans UX before code · init writes PRODUCT.md · document writes DESIGN.md · extract pulls repeated patterns into your design system

 The 24th, craft , is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type /impeccable alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: impeccable.style/docs .

 On Codex, open /skills or type $impeccable instead of the slash command.

 Live mode

 /impeccable live opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. Iterate in the browser .

 Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your package.json 's optional impeccable:manual-edit-validate script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo.

 Three ways to run the detector

 In your agent. The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. Automatic design checks .

 In CI or your terminal. The CLI needs no agent:

 npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory
npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge)
npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output
npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations
npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description

 Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173 .

 Exit code 2 means findings, 1 means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font" . To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: <!-- impeccable-disable overused-font: exported brand doc --> . Run a detector scan · Configuration and ignores .

 In your browser. The Chrome extension overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. Review with a visual overlay .

 Installation

 npx impeccable install

 The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. npx impeccable update refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass --providers=claude,codex,cursor and --scope=project|global .

 Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open /hooks and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run /hooks-trust or launch with --trust . In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook once. Allow the hook in your harness .

 Node is only needed for npx . The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into ~/.impeccable/bin/ .

 Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins
 Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable , then open /plugin and install Impeccable.

 GitHub Copilot in VS Code: install Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace or run code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable . Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. Details .

 Grok Build: grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust installs the skill, agents, and hook.

 Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team)
 git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable
npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor

 Commit .gitmodules , the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run git submodule update --init --recursive . To upgrade, run git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable , rerun the link command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass --force .

 Manual copy, no Node required
 Download the ZIP for your tool from impeccable.style , or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy skills/impeccable from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder.

 Tool
 Repo folder
 Global skills folder

 Claude Code
 .claude/
 ~/.claude/skills/

 Cursor
 .cursor/

 Codex CLI, Replit Agent
 .agents/
 ~/.agents/skills/

 Devin
 .devin/
 ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/

 GitHub Copilot
 .github/

 Gemini CLI
 .gemini/

 Google Antigravity
 .agent/
 ~/.gemini/config/skills/

 OpenCode
 .opencode/

 Grok Build
 .grok/
 ~/.grok/skills/

 Hermes Agent
 .hermes/
 ${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/

 DeepSeek Harness
 .dsh/
 ${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/

 Pi
 .pi/

 Qoder
 .qoder/
 ~/.qoder/skills/

 Rovo Dev
 .rovodev/
 ~/.rovodev/skills/

 Mistral Vibe
 .vibe/
 ~/.vibe/skills/

 Trae
 .trae/
 ~/.trae/skills/

 Trae China
 .trae-cn/
 ~/.trae-cn/skills/

 For example: mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/ .

 Notes:

- A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run npx impeccable install to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path.

- OpenCode also needs .opencode/commands/impeccable.md copied into your project's .opencode/commands/ to provide /impeccable .

- Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run hermes skills trust from the project root. Global installs need no trust step.

- Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the Cursor and Gemini CLI skills docs.

- Restart Trae after copying.

- impeccable install and update manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when DSH_HOME is inside your home directory.

 Project files and git

 Impeccable writes its working files under .impeccable/ . A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: config.json , live/config.json , design.json , surfaces/*.md , and critique/*.md . Keep PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state.

 Copy the .gitignore entries
 # impeccable-ignore-start
 # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides.
 # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace.
 # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json,
 # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md.
 ** / .impeccable / config.local.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.cache.json
 ** / .impeccable / hook.pending.json
 ** / .impeccable / * .png
 ** / .impeccable / review /
 ** / .impeccable / questions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / server.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / sessions /
 ** / .impeccable / live / previews /
 ** / .impeccable / live / annotations /
 ** / .impeccable / live / cache /
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-apply-transaction.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-events.jsonl
 ** / .impeccable / live / manual-edit-evidence /
 ** / .impeccable / live / pending-manual-edits.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json
 ** / .impeccable / live / * .png
 # impeccable-ignore-end

 The folders that hold decision-round state ( .impeccable/questions/ , .impeccable/mocks/worlds/ ) also ignore themselves. A .gitignore can't untrack a file git already tracks; if you committed one earlier, run git rm --cached <path> .

 Good to know

 Build path. For new landing pages and showcase surfaces, Impeccable can generate a full-fidelity comp first and build to match it (bolder, slower), or build straight in code (leaner, faster). App screens and documents are always built in code. init asks once and saves the answer as buildPath in .impeccable/...

representativeRepos.readmeText:
T3 Code

 T3 Code is an "agent harness control surface". It enables control of the agents on your machine with a best-in-class mobile app ( iOS , Android ), web app and Electron-based desktop app .

 Works with your subscriptions on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, and fx. If they're set up on your computer, T3 Code can control them.

 "Wait, what are you selling me?"

 Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar.

 We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the editor that you want.

 Installation

 Warning
 T3 Code currently supports Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity, and fx. Install and authenticate at least one provider before use:

- Codex: install Codex CLI and run codex login

- Claude: install Claude Code and run claude auth login

- Cursor: install Cursor CLI and run agent login

- Grok Build: install Grok Build CLI and run grok login

- OpenCode: install OpenCode and run opencode auth login

- Antigravity: enable it in Settings, then use Install Antigravity and Sign in with Google . No CLI is required.

- fx: install fx and run fx login on the machine running the T3 Code server ( setup guide )

 Command line

 curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh

 On Windows, in PowerShell:

 irm https: // t3.codes / install.ps1 | iex

 Then run t3 to start the server and open the local web app. t3 service install keeps it running in the background, t3 update moves to a newer release, and t3 --help has the full reference.

 To try it once without installing, run npx t3@latest instead.

 Desktop app

 Install the latest version of the desktop app from GitHub Releases , or from your favorite package registry:

 Windows ( winget )

 winget install T3Tools.T3Code

 Windows ( scoop )

 scoop install extras/t3code

 macOS (Homebrew)

 brew install --cask t3-code

 Debian, Ubuntu ( .deb )

 Download the .deb from GitHub Releases , then:

 sudo apt install ./T3-Code- * .deb

 Arch Linux (AUR)

 Stable:

 yay -S t3code-bin

 Nightly:

 yay -S t3code-nightly-bin

 The AUR packaging is maintained in this repository under packaging/aur .

 Nix (nixpkgs)

 nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code

 The package is maintained in nixpkgs
and includes the desktop app ( t3code-desktop ) and the t3 command.
See Nix installation for NixOS configuration and updates.

 Some notes

 We are very very early in this project. Expect bugs.

 We are (mostly) not accepting contributions yet. Small fixes may be considered. Big features will not be.

 Documentation

 Full docs live in docs/ . There's no docs site yet.

- FAQ

- Install and first run

- Permission modes

- Keyboard shortcuts

- Project settings

- Appearance preferences

- Remote access from a phone or another machine

- Connect Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT and other agents over MCP

- Keeping app and server in sync

- Source control integrations

- Multiple accounts: Codex · Claude

- Run T3 Code as a background service

 Building from source? Start at docs/internals/overview.md .

 If you REALLY want to contribute still.... read this first

 Install vp

 T3 Code uses Vite+ so you'll need to install the global vp command-line tool.

 macOS / Linux

 curl -fsSL https://vite.plus | bash

 Windows

 irm https://vite.plus/ps1 | iex

 Checkout their getting started guide for more information: https://viteplus.dev/guide/

 Install dependencies

 vp i

 Read CONTRIBUTING.md before reporting a bug or opening a PR.

 Have a feature request? Start an Ideas discussion .

 Need support? Join the Discord .
